liz_support: FYI — multiple customers in EU1 reporting 502/504s for hosted API since ~09:12 UTC. Symptoms: streaming completions and large-embeddings failing. Escalations and tickets: #12345, #12367. sample traces: trace=abc123, trace=def456

matt_eng_sre: On it. Can you paste 1) a failing curl/client sample and 2) edge log snippets? I'll start checking ingress and LB metrics.

liz_support: curl sample:
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"hello"}' \
  https://api.eu1.redwood.ai/v1/chat
```
edge log excerpt:
`2026/03/20 09:12:34 [error] 1234#0: *56789 upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out) while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.4.5.6, server: api.eu1.redwood.ai, request: "POST /v1/chat HTTP/2.0"`

deploy-bot: nginx-config-rollout v1.8 -> v1.9 completed on eu1 at 09:10 UTC (canary=0.1 -> global) :rocket:

ana_runtime: I see a clear spike in edge-proxy 504s starting at 09:12 (matches traces). Logs show a lot of h2 keepalive resets and `upstream prematurely closed connection` entries. Model servers show normal CPU and token p95, so it's proxy/edge related. Quick graph: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/edge/504-spike

matt_eng_sre: @ana_runtime good catch. I pulled the nginx diff from the rollout. Notable changes in v1.9: `proxy_read_timeout` reduced from `60s` -> `30s`, and `keepalive_timeout 75s` was removed (was previously present). That would shorten how long streaming responses can be read and may cause mid-stream 504s for longer completions. :thinking_face:

liz_support: Customers are blocked and asking for an ETA. Can we rollback the config?

matt_eng_sre: Rolling back nginx-config v1.9 -> v1.8 on eu1 now. Command used: `deploy rollback nginx-config eu1 --to v1.8`

oncall-bot: Rollback started by matt_eng_sre at 09:17 UTC. Deploy ID: deploy-7890

matt_eng_sre: Rollback completed at 09:18 UTC. Observability: 504 rate dropped toward baseline by 09:21 UTC; streaming requests resumed. Hotfix plan: re-add `keepalive_timeout 75s` and restore `proxy_read_timeout 60s`, then run a canary that simulates long-lived streaming (`curl --http2` with chunked response). :white_check_mark:

kevin_prod: Postmortem items — add a preflight test for long-lived streams in the nginx rollout pipeline, gate global rollout on a 1% canary that runs streaming repros, and update the runbook to include quick rollback steps and the `proxy_read_timeout` checklist.

liz_support: Confirmed with the customers that traffic is back and we updated the tickets with credits. Next steps: create a repeated test in CI that opens 500 concurrent streaming sessions against any nginx config change and fails the rollout if p50/p95 token latency or 5xx rate increases. I'll file the follow-up tasks.

(links to artifacts, traces, and the rollback diff saved in the ticket attachments)
